title: Weight: Grams and Kilograms
seo_title: Weight – Primary 3 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Measure weight in grams and kilograms; read weighing scales; compare weights; solve simple weight problems. (summary of the NERDC Primary 3 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 3 maths worksheets on weight: grams and kilograms, reading weighing scales, balances, comparing and estimating weights. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Heavy things in kg, light things in g.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • We measure weight in grams (g) and kilograms (kg). 1 kg = 1,000 g.
  • Light things like a pencil are measured in grams. Heavy things like a bag of rice are in kilograms.
  • On a balance, the heavier side goes down.

Examples

Example

A bag of rice weighs 5 kg and a bag of beans weighs 3 kg

5 + 3

Answer: 8 kg altogether

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Reading the wrong scaleFind the value of each mark.
Thinking big means heavyA big pillow can be light.
Mixing g and kgChange to the same unit.

items.q: How many grams are in 1 kilogram?
items.e: Kilo means 1,000. So 1 kg = 1,000 g.

items.q: What is the best estimate for the mass of a bag of sugar?
items.e: A bag of sugar is about 1 kilogram. 1 g is about the mass of a paper clip.

items.q: What is the best estimate for the mass of an apple?
items.e: An apple is light, about 100 grams. 100 kg is heavier than a grown-up.

items.q: What is the best estimate for the mass of a Primary 3 child?
items.e: A Primary 3 child is about 25 kilograms. 25 g is lighter than a bar of chocolate.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a bag of carrots. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 100 g. There are 2 spaces between numbers, so each mark is 100 ÷ 2 = 50 g. The needle is 1 mark past 300: 300 + 50 = 350 g.

items.e: Each kilogram is split into 2 equal spaces. 1 kg = 1,000 g, so each mark is 1,000 ÷ 2 = 500 g. The needle is 1 mark past 2 kg: 2 kg + 500 g = 2 kg 500 g.

items.q: The scale shows a bag of flour. How much more flour is needed to make 1 kg?

items.q: Look at the pan balance. Which object is heavier?
items.e: The left side is lower. The lower pan holds the heavier object, so the watermelon is heavier and the orange is lighter.

items.q: Look at the pan balance. Which object is lighter?
items.e: The right side is lower. The lower pan holds the heavier object, so the bowling ball is heavier and the beach ball is lighter. A bigger object is not always heavier.

items.q: The pan balance is level. What is the mass of the apple?
items.e: The pans are level, so the apple has the same mass as the weights: 100 + 50 = 150 g.

items.q: The pan balance is level. What is the mass of the orange?
items.e: The pans are level, so the orange has the same mass as the weights: 100 + 50 + 50 = 200 g.

items.q: The pan balance is level. What is the mass of the pumpkin?

items.q: The pan balance is level. The lemons all have the same mass. What is the mass of 1 lemon?
items.e: The weight shows 500 g for all 5 lemons. Share it equally: 500 ÷ 5 = 100 g.

items.q: The pan balance is level. The melons all have the same mass. What is the mass of 1 melon?
items.e: The weights show 2 + 2 = 4 kg for both melons. Share it equally: 4 ÷ 2 = 2 kg.

items.q: The pan balance is level. The tennis balls all have the same mass. What is the mass of 1 tennis ball?
items.e: The weights show 200 + 20 + 20 = 240 g for all 4 tennis balls. Share it equally: 240 ÷ 4 = 60 g.

items.q: The pan balance is level. The apples all have the same mass. What is the mass of 1 apple?
items.e: The weights show 500 + 100 = 600 g for all 4 apples. Share it equally: 600 ÷ 4 = 150 g.

items.q: The pan balance is level. The eggs all have the same mass. What is the mass of 1 egg?
items.e: The weights show 100 + 50 = 150 g for all 3 eggs. Share it equally: 150 ÷ 3 = 50 g.

items.q: The pan balance is level. What is the mass of the sack of potatoes?
items.e: The right pan has 5 kg. The left pan has the sack of potatoes and 1 kg. 5 − 1 = 4 kg for the sack of potatoes.

items.q: The pan balance is level. What is the mass of the box of crayons?
items.e: The right pan has 200 g. The left pan has the box of crayons and 50 g. 200 − 50 = 150 g for the box of crayons.

items.q: The pan balance is level. What is the mass of the pineapple?
items.e: The right pan has 3 kg. The left pan has the pineapple and 1 kg. 3 − 1 = 2 kg for the pineapple.

items.q: The pan balance is level. What is the mass of the jar of jam?
items.e: The right pan has 400 g. The left pan has the jar of jam and 50 g. 400 − 50 = 350 g for the jar of jam.

items.q: Ibrahim has 85 cm of ribbon. He cuts off 30 cm. How much ribbon is left?
items.e: Cutting off means subtract: 85 − 30 = 55 cm.

items.q: Chidi has two pieces of ribbon. One is 45 cm long. The other is 38 cm long. How much ribbon is there altogether?
items.e: Add: 45 + 38. 5 + 8 = 13, so exchange 10 units for 1 ten. 45 + 38 = 83 cm.

items.q: A sunflower was 35 cm tall. It grew 18 cm more. How tall is it now?
items.e: Add: 35 + 18 = 53 cm. Remember to exchange: 5 + 8 = 13.

items.q: Blessing builds a train track 3 m long. She adds 1 m 50 cm more track. How long is the track now?
items.e: Add the metres: 3 m + 1 m = 4 m. Then add the 50 cm. The track is 4 m 50 cm long.

items.q: Bisi is 1 m 25 cm tall. Ife is 1 m 10 cm tall. How much taller is Bisi?
items.e: Both are 1 m and some more. Compare the centimetres: 25 − 10 = 15 cm.

items.q: Amaka has 1 m 40 cm of string. She ties on 80 cm more. How long is the string now?
items.e: 40 cm + 80 cm = 120 cm = 1 m 20 cm. Add this to 1 m: 1 m + 1 m 20 cm = 2 m 20 cm.

items.q: Ngozi needs 250 g of flour for a cake and 175 g of flour for biscuits. How much flour does she need altogether?
items.e: Add: 250 + 175. 5 tens + 7 tens = 12 tens, so exchange 10 tens for 1 hundred. 250 + 175 = 425 g.

items.q: Hauwa has a 1 kg bag of flour. She uses 350 g to bake bread. How much flour is left?
A bag of apples weighs 600 g. A bag of oranges weighs 450 g. How much do they weigh altogether?
A parcel can weigh up to 2 kg. Mum's parcel weighs 1 kg 300 g. How much more can she put in it?
Tobi's school bag weighs 2 kg. He puts in a lunchbox that weighs 500 g. How much does the bag weigh now?
items.e: Add the grams to the kilograms: 2 kg + 500 g = 2 kg 500 g.

items.q: Nkechi has a 500 ml bottle of water. She drinks 175 ml. How much water is left?
items.e: Subtract: 500 − 175. Exchange across the zeros: 500 − 175 = 325 ml. Check: 325 + 175 = 500.

items.q: A recipe needs 300 ml of milk. Kayode has 1 l of milk. How much milk is left after making the recipe?
For a party, Dad buys a 1 l carton of juice and a 500 ml carton of juice. How much juice is there altogether?
items.e: Add the millilitres to the litres: 1 l + 500 ml = 1 l 500 ml (1,500 ml).

items.q: For a party, a jug holds 1 l of squash. Four cups of 200 ml are poured. How much squash is left in the jug?
At a party there are 2 l of orange juice. The children drink 1 l 400 ml. How much juice is left?
A fish tank has 5 l of water. 2 l 500 ml more is added. How much water is in the tank now?
items.e: Add the litres: 5 l + 2 l = 7 l. Then add the 500 ml: 7 l 500 ml.

items.q: Sani needs ribbon to wrap presents. He has 2 m of ribbon and uses 75 cm. How much ribbon is left?
items.e: 2 m = 200 cm. Subtract: 200 − 75 = 125 cm. 125 cm = 1 m 25 cm.

items.q: On inter-house sports, Ifeanyi jumps 1 m 85 cm. Chinedu jumps 2 m 10 cm. How much further does Chinedu jump?
items.e: 1 m 85 cm = 185 cm and 2 m 10 cm = 210 cm. Count on: 185 → 200 is 15 cm, 200 → 210 is 10 cm. 15 + 10 = 25 cm.

items.q: A brown worm is 45 mm long. A pink worm is 6 cm long. Which worm is longer, and by how much?
items.e: 6 cm = 60 mm. 60 mm is more than 45 mm, so the pink worm is longer. 60 − 45 = 15 mm. Do not take 6 from 45: change to the same unit first.
